A compositor sets type one sort at a time. The copy line is pinned above the case, the lead sorts are lying loose in the forme, and the only tool is a blank quad you can shove them with.
COMPOSITOR is a Game Boy ROM, running in your browser. This is the free demo: eight formes of the forty, a 32,768 byte demo cartridge running in an emulator on the page.
EVERY FORME SHIPS WITH ITS PROVED SHORTEST SETTING

This is the part that is not a figure of speech. Each forme was generated and then searched exhaustively, over every arrangement the board can reach, for the shortest sequence of pushes that sets the line. That number is BEST in the footer while you play.
It is not a par, and it is not the length of the first solution the generator stumbled on. It is the minimum, and there is no better one. When you match BEST you have found a shortest solution.

Then every forme was played to a set line on this exact ROM by a bot, in exactly its proved number of pushes, before the cartridge was allowed out. A solver that is right about a game the ROM is not playing would be worth nothing, so the two are checked against each other rather than trusted separately.
THE ORDER IS FINAL, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE GAME

A sort can only be pushed, never pulled, and there is no row beneath the composing stick to stand in. Two sorts delivered into the stick in the wrong order can never be swapped. A forme can be permanently dead with everything still on screen and nothing obviously wrong.

That is why B undoes and SELECT restarts. They are not conveniences. The solver proved the deadlock exists before a line of the game was written, and without them the cartridge would silently brick a board and never tell you.
TWENTY SIX LETTERS, DRAWN AS DATA
Every letterform is authored pixel by pixel for a sixteen pixel body in the four shades the hardware has, lit on the top left and shadowed on the bottom right, the printing face inset behind a bevel.

The screens are composed at runtime out of those parts, so forty distinct formes exist in the full game and not one of them is stored as a picture. There is no sprite sheet and no atlas. That is how the whole thing fits in 32 KB alongside the solver's answers and the sound driver.

A sort standing in its own place in the line lights up whole, in the brightest shade on the screen, so you can always see how far along you are without reading a number. The frame and the edges of the other sorts use that shade too, as thin lines; only a set sort is filled with it.
WHAT WAS TESTED, AND WHAT WAS NOT

The cartridge was developed and verified in the emulator binjgb, driven a frame at a time from a cold boot, with the screen it drew compared pixel for pixel against a separate reference renderer. It has not been run on physical hardware. Nobody here owns a Game Boy or a flash cart, so the honest claim is the format and the emulator, not a compatibility badge. If you own the hardware and you run it, say how it went and we will put that here.
THE FULL CARTRIDGE
This demo is eight formes, and after the eighth it says so. The full cartridge is forty, ordered from eight pushes to eighteen, with a forme picker, an ending and a credits screen, and it is on itch.

Controls: on the title, the left and right arrows choose the forme and Enter begins; Right Shift switches the sound. On a forme, the arrows walk the quad, Z undoes a push, Right Shift restarts the forme, Enter goes back to the title, and X continues once a line is set.

New in 1.1.0: a forme picker, the forme number on screen, an ending and credits, a demo that ends with a card, the sound when a line is set (it was silent), sound switched on the title instead of on A, and undo that stays correct past 64 pushes.
Sound is the console's own four hardware channels, driven by register writes. No samples.

Made by Core Systems Asset Factory. GBDK-2020 C written by AI, no engine, no template, no stock art. AI disclosure: code yes, graphics yes, text and dialogue yes (every word on screen; there is no story), sounds no. Tags follow.
